The finite-difference check confirms the signs. A unit of glucose-equivalent injection moves the slot stream about 0.31 along the real glucose-reading direction (10th to 90th percentile 0.14 to 0.48), and the MAP injection about 0.29 along the MAP direction. The full edit is saved: z_post.0/.2 weights and biases, plus z_in.weight. Now the real test is the evaluation's rollout on the same 100 tuning stays as my first dose_edit run, where I have per-stay-hour targets (insulin ×2 ≈ −13.8, ×½ ≈ +6.9; NE ×2 ≈ +4.6, ×½ ≈ −2.3). Running original and edited models side by side gives the edit's effect with common random numbers. I expect the edited effects to be clearly larger than the original's (−2.15 / +0.34) and in the right direction. The size tells me how to rescale κ_A and κ_B. No change, or a wrong sign, would refute the pathway.
